overview: A bacterial communication mechanism and one of its major downstream outcomes, often discussed together but conceptually distinct.
genZNote: Quorum sensing is the group chat. Biofilm is the group project they build together.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A cell-density-dependent signaling process in which bacteria produce and detect small diffusible molecules (autoinducers) to coordinate gene expression.
aspects.valueB: The process by which bacteria attach to a surface and each other, encased in a self-produced extracellular polymeric matrix.

aspects.label: Relationship Between the Two
aspects.valueA: Often triggers biofilm formation once a population reaches a threshold density.
aspects.valueB: Frequently regulated (initiated, matured, or dispersed) by quorum-sensing signals.

aspects.label: Molecular Basis
aspects.valueA: Autoinducer molecules (e.g. AHLs in Gram-negatives, autoinducing peptides in Gram-positives) bind receptors to alter transcription.
aspects.valueB: Extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix of polysaccharides, proteins, and eDNA encasing the bacterial community.

aspects.label: Clinical Relevance
aspects.valueA: A target for anti-virulence therapies aiming to block bacterial coordination without directly killing bacteria.
aspects.valueB: Associated with chronic infections and device-related infections resistant to antibiotics and host defenses.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Chemical signaling mechanism sensing population density.
aspects.valueB: Structural, matrix-encased bacterial community, often a result of that signaling.
